title: POC scoping: route NLP model shortlist - Horizon Transit
next_steps: Redwood to send benchmark plan + sample prompt sets
Horizon Transit to share a 1-week production trace and 500 sample route docs
Schedule SE-led bench run (2 weeks) and follow-up sync
action_items: Maya Chen | Share benchmark template + prompt bank | 2025-02-03
Lina Gomez | Provide sanitized production trace & 500 sample documents | 2025-01-31
Ethan Park | Run quick latency/throughput sanity run on 3 shortlisted models and share results | 2025-02-10
summary: Discovery + POC scoping to pick an open-model shortlist for multilingual route extraction and scheduling heuristics. Focus on accuracy on Spanish/Portuguese route names, 100–300ms p50 latency target for interactive UI, and pilot timeline of ~8 weeks after bench validation.
meeting_header: Date: 2025-01-28 14:00 PST; Duration: 52 minutes; Location: Zoom; Recording: yes; Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Ethan Park (Redwood SE), Lina Gomez (Head of ML, Horizon Transit), Raj Patel (Platform Lead), Sofia Marino (Product PM)
transcript:
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call?
[00:07] Lina: Lina here.
[00:09] Raj: Raj on the line.
[00:12] Sofia: Sofia here.
[00:15] Ethan: Ethan from Redwood. Morning/afternoon all.
[00:20] Maya: Great, goal for today is to scope the POC: success criteria, rough workload sizing, and pick a short list of open models to bench. We'll also note security needs. Sound right?
[00:33] Sofia: Yep. We're trying to move from a rules-based extractor to an ML-first pipeline for route parsing across English, Spanish, Portuguese. Priority is accuracy on stop names and travel directions, and latency for our agent UI.
[00:47] Lina: I'll add we need model outputs to be deterministic-ish for downstream scheduling. And we have to keep PII out - so sanitized bench data is needed.
[00:56] Raj: On infra side we have a Kubernetes cluster in GCP, but for POC we want Redwood hosted first, then Dedicated or VPC for pilot.
[01:07] Ethan: Noted. For Hosted vs Dedicated, we typically recommend starting hosted to get bench signal, then move to Dedicated if throughput or compliance requires it.
[01:20] Maya: Can we go into success criteria? What are your hard gates?
[01:26] Sofia: Hard gates: >92% F1 on token-level route extraction for English and Spanish, and p50 latency under 300ms for the interactive UI. P95 ideally under 800ms. Cost targets are soft but important.
[01:41] Lina: Also need at least basic support for Portuguese; if we can't hit 92% there, we'll accept 85% as long as improvement curve is clear.
[01:51] Raj: From ops: max concurrent interactive users ~150, background batch jobs for nightly reconciliation about 2000 docs/hour.
[02:01] Ethan: Cool. That gives us target QPS and batch throughput to size hardware. For interactive requests what's your average tokens per request?
[02:09] Sofia: Roughly 120 tokens per request — we're sending a short history plus current route doc.
[02:16] Lina: Some docs are noisy — images OCRed, so lots of odd tokens.
[02:21] Maya: Great. We'll include noise in the bench. On models: Ethan, can you walk through candidate open models?
[02:28] Ethan: Sure. We're thinking of a pragmatic shortlist: Llama 2 13B (quantized variants), Mistral 7B-instruct variants, Phi-3 12B, and a smaller instruction-tuned 7B for latency-sensitive paths. You might also consider MPT variants for long context, though probably overkill here.
[02:48] Lina: Any thoughts on Falcon? We saw mixed results in our earlier tests.
[02:52] Ethan: Falcon-40B is strong but costly. For our POC we want models that balance accuracy and fast kernels on NVIDIA A10/A100 or on AMP-like quantized runtimes. Also note: open names sometimes transcribed — like 'Phi-3' may show up as fee-three in transcriptions.
[03:07] Raj: Wanted to flag enterprise constraints — we need SOC2 + VPC during pilot. Also key management for encryption.
[03:15] Maya: Redwood supports KMS integrations and VPC/private deployments; we'll include a security appendix.
[03:22] Sofia: Benchmarks: what metrics will you collect in the 2-week bench?
[03:27] Ethan: We propose accuracy (token F1, exact-match for key fields), latency (p50/p95), throughput under batching, GPU utilization, and cost per 1k requests. We'll run inference with your sanitized trace to get realistic distribution.
[03:41] Lina: For accuracy, can we also include confusion matrix for stop name types (station, street, landmark)? That's critical for product routing heuristics.
[03:49] Ethan: Yes, we'll add that to the eval.
[03:52] Maya: Timelines — what do you want?
[03:55] Sofia: We want a rapid bench within 2 weeks and then a pilot of 6–8 weeks if the bench passes.
[04:03] Maya: That aligns with our standard: 2-week bench, then pilot planning. We'll package a bench plan today and send prompts.
[04:09] Raj: On workload sizing, if p50 is 300ms and 150 concurrent users, can you give a rough GPU estimate?
[04:17] Ethan: Rough back-of-envelope: for 13B quantized to int8 on A10s, you might get ~40–60 qps per GPU for small batches (1–4). For stricter 150 concurrent interactive users with low latency, you'd likely need 3–4 GPUs to have headroom depending on batching. We'll provide a more precise sizing after bench.
[04:34] Lina: If we use a smaller 7B model for interactive and a larger 13B for nightly batch reconciliation, is that a recommended hybrid approach?
[04:42] Ethan: Yes, hybrid routing is common — small low-latency models for interactive, heavier models for offline reconciliation. Redwood routing policies can handle automatic fallbacks.
[04:51] Sofia: Are there quality tradeoffs with quantization that we should expect?
[04:55] Ethan: Some drop in exact-match for entity spans with aggressive quant. Usually 1–3% F1 drop moving from fp16 to int8/4 quant. We'll surface quantization-aware evals.
[05:06] Maya: Any regulatory or data residency concerns?
[05:09] Raj: We're operating across LATAM and EU customers; retention and residency require us to keep certain records in-region for EU. Pilot must allow VPC or private deployment in EU region later.
[05:21] Ethan: Redwood supports region pinning and private deployments; we'll note the constraint.
[05:27] Maya: Let's talk failure modes — how user experience should degrade if model latency spikes.
[05:31] Sofia: For the agent UI, we prefer a fast graceful fallback: show partial parse with an edit option, and fallback to a rules-based extractor if model times out.
[05:41] Lina: We'll provide a list of top 10 frequent route patterns so you can test heuristics.
[05:46] Ethan: Perfect. On data sharing: please send sanitized data via approved S3 bucket or secure upload; do not email PII.
[05:54] Raj: We'll create a sanitized export this week.
[05:57] Maya: Bench plan details: we'll run 3 model variants, each with: interactive latency test, batch throughput test, and accuracy on labeled set. Do we need to include multilingual prompts in the bench?
[06:09] Lina: Absolutely — split bench: 60% English, 25% Spanish, 15% Portuguese. Include code-switching examples.
[06:17] Ethan: Noted. For metrics thresholds: 92% F1 English/Spanish, 85% Portuguese acceptable baseline. p50 < 300ms for the interactive model.
[06:26] Sofia: How will you handle deterministic outputs? We sometimes need the same output for the same input across calls.
[06:32] Ethan: We can run models with temperature=0 and top_p cutoff to reduce stochasticity. Also caching strategies for prefix KV cache will help. We'll record settings and test determinism in bench.
[06:44] Maya: Any questions on pricing or cost transparency?
[06:47] Raj: We'd like a clear per-inference cost estimate for both hosted and dedicated scenarios.
[06:52] Maya: We'll include per-token cost estimates plus GPU amortized cost for Dedicated.
[06:58] Lina: For the shortlist, can you list exact checkpoints you'll test?
[07:02] Ethan: We'll test: Llama-2-13b-instruct (quantized v1), Mistral-Instruct-7B (we'll pick the instruction tuned), Phi-3-12B (open checkpoint), and a Llama/Mistral 7B low-latency variant. We'll note that names sometimes vary across hubs and we'll use Redwood-verified checkpoints.
[07:20] Sofia: Any preference on tokenizers or text normalization? Our OCR includes diacritics sometimes missing.
[07:26] Lina: We normalize to NFC but keep accents where possible; bench should include variants.
[07:31] Ethan: We'll include normalization ablations.
[07:34] Maya: Security appendix — we'll attach SOC2 cert, penetration test summary, and VPC prep checklist.
[07:40] Raj: Good. For pilot, expected timeline if bench passes: provisioning and pilot kickoff in 2 weeks, 6–8 week pilot, then decision.
[07:50] Maya: So timeline summary: Bench run: 2 weeks starting once we get data (Lina target 2025-01-31). SE bench results and sizing: ~week of 2025-02-10. Pilot kickoff ideally 2025-02-17.
[07:59] Sofia: That works.
[08:02] Ethan: I'll note some risk: OCR noise may dominate errors; better upstream OCR cleanup may improve F1 more than model swap.
[08:12] Lina: We're aware and have a small OCR team investigating.
[08:15] Maya: Ok let's capture action items — we already listed a few. Any other asks?
[08:20] Sofia: If you can include a short doc on hybrid routing patterns that would help our architects.
[08:25] Maya: We'll include that.
[08:27] Raj: Also price band for Dedicated GPUs (monthly) versus hosted per-inference to compare.
[08:33] Maya: Noted.
[08:35] Maya: Anything else?
[08:36] Lina: No, thanks.
[08:38] Maya: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the bench plan and calendar invites for the bench kickoff.
[08:43] Sofia: Thanks.
[08:45] (meeting ends)

Notes about transcript: occasional filler, some entity names may be transcribed incorrectly (e.g., Mistral -> Mystral). We intentionally kept timestamps approximate; full bench plan will be attached as a separate doc link.
